subject: Clarify ad-targeting signals and provide subprocessor evidence
messages:
From: Amanda Lopez <amanda.lopez@acmeretail.com>
To: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai, Tom Reynolds <treynolds@acmeretail.com>
Date: 2026-08-11T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Clarify ad-targeting signals + subprocessor list

Hi Vivek —

Thanks for the demo yesterday. A couple of compliance follow-ups from our privacy and procurement teams before we move into procurement:

1) Classification of ad-targeting signals under CCPA/CPRA — does Redwood consider the signals we would send (hashed customer IDs + inferred cohort tags) to be a “sale” or outside sale classification if used for targeted advertising by our marketing team? We need a short written position to share with Acme legal.

2) Subprocessor evidence — please provide a current list of subprocessors that will touch PII (names/emails/ids) and for each: country, role (hosting/logging/analytics), whether they have access to raw IDs, and whether they are covered by SOC2 or equivalent.

3) Onshore fallback and telemetry — our security team wants an estimate of how quickly you can failover telemetry/event processing to a US-only cluster in the event of regulatory/contractual requirements.

Can you also attach your SOC2 report or a link and a redline-friendly DPA exhibit that addresses CPRA-specific language (service provider vs. third party, sale definition, targeted advertising prohibition)? Attached is our standard RFI template for background.

Thanks — please loop in your privacy folks.

Amanda Lopez
Sr. Privacy Counsel | Acme Retail, Inc.
Attachments: Acme_RFI_template.pdf

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Amanda Lopez <amanda.lopez@acmeretail.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>, Tom Reynolds <treynolds@acmeretail.com>
Date: 2026-08-11T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify ad-targeting signals + subprocessor list

Amanda — thanks for the note and the RFI. Taking point on coordination. Monica (security) and Rachel (privacy) are copied to respond with the subprocessor inventory and a recommended CPRA/CPPA exhibit.

Short answers up front: we do not treat deterministic hashed IDs used for cohorting as a ‘sale’ in our standard position; we treat our advertising pipeline as a service provider flow (no monetization of customer lists). I’ll let Rachel provide the legal wording and Monica provide the inventory and technical controls.

Quick ask: can Acme confirm whether the cohorts will be used for first-party audience matching only, or if you intend to syndicate audiences to external DSPs/advertisers? That changes a couple of controls and the routing (and could affect classification).

Timeline: we should be able to share the subprocessor list and SOC2 link by end-of-day today and a redline DPA exhibit tomorrow.

— Vivek
Head of Customer Success | Redwood Inference

Hi Amanda — attaching the current subprocessor export and a short technical note (see attachments). Key points: 

- Subprocessors (summary):
  • CloudHostCo (US) — hosting/compute — has access to decrypted runtime data; SOC2 Type II covered.
  • CacheFlow Systems (US) — persistent KV cache for inference acceleration — only stores hashed IDs and model-side features; access controlled via IAM.
  • TelemetryHub (US/CA) — telemetry aggregation and dashboards — receives event-level telemetry (no long-term storage of raw IDs; aggregated within 24 hours).
  • LogArchive Partners (US/EU) — backup storage — encrypted at rest; access limited to emergency restore.

- Access to raw IDs: only CloudHostCo may see decrypted tokens in certain dedicated/private deployments; in hosted mode we hash/encrypt before persistent storage. For ad-targeting pipelines we persist hashed identifiers and cohort labels, not cleartext emails.

- Telemetry onshore fallback: for US-only processing we can route telemetry and event pipelines to a US-only cluster. Planned SLA for failover is 72 hours for configuration + 24 hours for data re-ingestion (96 hours total) for the current infra; for Dedicated customers we can shorten this to 24–48 hours depending on contracted capacity.

- Encryption & retention: all storage encrypted at rest (AES-256); keys are customer-separable in Dedicated and Private deployments. Default retention: 90 days for event telemetry; configurable for enterprise.

Attachments: subprocessors_v2.csv, telemetry-dataflow.png

If you need per-subprocessor SOC2 statements, we can request vendor attestations — tell us which vendors you care most about and we’ll prioritize.

— Monica
Security Engineering Manager | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Clarify ad-targeting signals + subprocessor list

Amanda — following up with recommended contract language and our position. High level: Redwood treats the processing of hashed customer identifiers and derived cohort labels, where Acme controls the audience definition and destination, as processing performed on behalf of the controller (service provider). We do not use customer lists for our own advertising or sell them to third parties.

Suggested CPRA exhibit snippets (summary):
• Service provider restriction: "Redwood shall process personal information solely on behalf of and at the direction of Customer and shall not retain, use, or disclose personal information for any purpose other than for the business purposes set forth in the Agreement."
• Targeted advertising: "If Customer directs Redwood to use personal information for targeted advertising, Customer represents and warrants it is a controller for advertising purposes; Redwood's standard position is to act as a Service Provider and not engage in targeted advertising on its own behalf. Any change to this behavior requires written agreement and an addendum."
• No sale: "Redwood does not sell Personal Information as defined under CCPA/CPRA. Sharing for advertising with third-party DSPs under Customer instruction will be treated as a narrow processing activity and not a sale where Redwood acts strictly as Service Provider and does not monetize the Personal Information."

Please find a draft redline attached: redwood-dpa-exhibit-draft.docx (we can provide a Word redline or a tracked doc in DocuSign). A couple of notes/questions:
- If Acme intends to syndicate audiences to external advertisers/DSPs that are not acting solely at Acme's direction, we may need to classify that flow differently and add explicit contractual constraints and audit rights.
- For CPRA-specific consumer rights (opt-out of targeted advertising) we recommend an exhibit that maps event-level signals to the opt-out mechanism and documents the opt-out honoring flow.

Happy to jump on a short call to walk through the redline tomorrow.

— Rachel Kim
Privacy Counsel | Redwood Inference
